 CORAM:
 HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE RAJNISH BHATNAGAR  OR % 19.10.2023 1.

This is a petition under Section 482 Cr.P.C. for quashing of FIR No.0578/2021, dated 22.06.2021 under Section 498A/406/34 IPC, registered at Police Station Bindapur, Delhi, and all proceedings emanating therefrom.

2. The brief facts of the case are that the petitioner No.1 and respondent No.2 got married on 21.02.2018 according to Hindu rites and ceremonies and they lived together as wife and husband with each other.
After the marriage, the disputes and differences arose between them and they started living separately since December 2018.
On 22.06.2021, the respondent No.2 got the above said FIR registered against the petitioners.
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 22/10/2023 at 02:26:07 3.
Counsel for the petitioners submits that during the pendency of the trial, the parties have settled the matter amicably in terms of the Memorandum of Understanding dated 04.04.2022.
Copy of the said MOU is placed on record.

Accordingly, the petition under Section 13- B(2) of the HMA Act was allowed and the marriage of the petitioner No.1 and respondent No.2 was dissolved vide decree Arun Kumar & Ors vs The State & Anr on 19 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/38693201/

sentences.text: . The copy of the decree is already on record.
4. Petitioner nos. 2, 3, 5, 6, 7, 8 & 9 are present in Court today.
Petitioner no. 1 is appearing through video-conferencing.
Exemption sought on behalf of petitioner no. 4 Suresh Kumar as he is not in a position to appear in the Court.
Medical certificate has been placed on record.
Respondent No.2 is also appearing through video conferencing and she has been identified by the IO.
I have interacted with the parties and they submit that they have settled their disputes.
Respondent No.2 admits that she has settled the matter amicably with the petitioners.
She further submits that the settlement has taken place voluntarily, without any force, pressure or coercion.
As per settlement, today, a demand draft of Rs. 2,00,000/- (bearing no. 976173 dated 16.10.2023, drawn on State Bank of India) has been received by the respondent no.2.

Respondent No.2 submits that nothing remains to be adjudicated further between them and she has no objection if the FIR in question is quashed.
5.
Learned APP for the State submits that in view of the settlement, the State has no objection if the FIR in question be quashed.
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 22/10/2023 at 02:26:07 6.
Keeping in view the above facts and circumstances, since the matter has been amicably settled between the parties, no useful purpose will be served by keeping the case pending.
It will be nothing but abuse of the process of law.

Consequentially, this petition is allowed and FIR No.0578/2021,
dated 22.06.2021 under Section 498A/406/34 IPC, registered at Police Station Bindapur, Delhi, and the proceedings emanating therefrom shall stand quashed.
7.
The present petition stands disposed of accordingly.
RAJNISH BHATNAGAR, J OCTOBER 19, 2023/akc
